question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type II region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{2}}^{y}(1-xy)\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{{y}^{2}}^{y}(1-xy)\,dx]\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[x-\frac{y{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{{y}^{2}}^{y}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{2}-({y}^{2}-\frac{{y}^{5}}{2}))\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{2}-{y}^{2}+\frac{{y}^{5}}{2})\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{2}-{y}^{2}+\frac{{y}^{5}}{2})\,dy & ={[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{y}^{4}}{8}-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}+\frac{{y}^{6}}{12}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{12}-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\end{aligned}
$$
